meta.source: Computed by npm run build:data from data/serial-formats.json and data/lifespans.json with assets/js/formulas.js
meta.notes: Default result and worked example are computed as of 2026-11-13 (site.json dateVerified). The live calculator uses the visitor's date.

default.headline: About 7.1 years old (built October 2019)
default.explain: That is about 55% of the 13-year typical life for this type (gas tank). Estimated remaining life: 2.9 to 7.9 years. (Example serial, as of 2026-11-13; type yours.)
default.formula:
Built: October 2019 (Rheem / Ruud code: week 43, year 2019)
Age = today − October 2019 = 7.1 years
Expected life (gas tank) = 10–15 years, typical 13; adjustments: none
Share used = 7.1 ÷ 13 = 55%
default.sources: Rheem date code: checked against Rheem/Ruud's own lookup. Lifespan: DOE 2024 water heater rule and DOE FEMP. Hardness, flushing and anode adjustments are our editorial assumptions. See the decoder checked against Rheem/Ruud, Bradford White and CPSC.

summaryRows.rule: two-digit week, then two-digit year; or two-digit month, then two-digit year
summaryRows.example: Q4319***** → week 43 of 2019 (Rheem/Ruud lookup: October 18, 2019); 0794****** → July 1994

summaryRows.rule: two-digit year, then two-digit week (2008 and later); or month letter, then two-digit year (up to 2008)

summaryRows.example: DF******* → June 1967, 1987, 2007 or 2027 (latest not in the future)

summaryRows.rule: two-digit year, then two-digit week (2008 and later); or month letter, then two-digit year (up to 2008)
summaryRows.example: 0904******* → 2009, week 4 (Energy Trust labels this example April 2009, which does not match its own year-week rule; we follow the rule); C05******* → March 2005

summaryRows.note: Whirlpool water heaters are made by American (part of A. O. Smith), so the American code is used.
